title: Per-Agent Artifacts keep governance amendments local instead of touching a shared rulebook
content:
A.6 establishes that each Agent Artifact governs the operations of a particular Agent, and A.6.1 collects those Artifacts per Agent.

The consequence is isolation. A shared rulebook makes every amendment a system-wide event: changing one Agent's parameters means editing a document binding all of them, so each change risks unintended effect elsewhere. Per-Agent Artifacts make the unit of amendment identical to the unit of authority.

The cost is duplication — common rules must be restated or cross-referenced across Artifacts, and can drift. The Atlas accepts that cost, relying on explicit cross-references (such as A.5.2.1.2's pointer to the shared Moderation policy) to re-share rules only where consistency actually matters.
description: Because each Artifact governs exactly one Agent's operations, amending one Agent's rules affects no other — bounding the blast radius of any change, at the cost of duplication.
